source.title: Gating creates slow modes and controls phase-space complexity in GRUs and LSTMs
source.authors: T. Can; K. Krishnamurthy; D. Schwab

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices. It is the titled study.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports preliminary GRU training results on sequential MNIST and evaluates training accuracy and epochs to a target accuracy across initialization regimes. This bears conceptually on initialization and training performance, but does not test the claim’s CIFAR classification error outcomes.
record.gate_note: The paper’s main results concern Jacobian spectra and fixed-point dynamics; cited results from other work are not rows. Appendix H reports GRU training accuracy and epochs to 75% on sequential MNIST, which bear on V4’s initialization/training-speed claim. Figure 4 values are not given numerically in the text, so the relevant outcomes are figure-only.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes gated recurrent networks and reports preliminary GRU training results. V4 concerns initialization in plain feedforward networks; GRU gate-variance comparisons do not test that version. Dynamical fixed-point stability and Jacobian spectra also do not measure optimization minima or learning-rate stability in V2 or V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the preliminary training findings, but omits the paper's main conclusion: gating shapes Jacobian spectra, slow modes, dynamical stability and fixed-point structure in randomly initialized GRUs and LSTMs. The authors associate improved GRU training with larger az and ah near, or slightly above, 2, while leaving a thorough account of dynamics during training to future work.
record.recipe_differences: Randomly initialized GRU gate and hidden-weight variances are varied in a sequential-MNIST task; the study does not use the feedforward benchmark recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: GRU update-gate variance az and hidden-weight variance ah change the plotted training accuracy and epochs to 75%; performance is best near ah = 2.0, and training appears harder further into the chaotic regime.

fits_no_version.finding: For a 256-unit GRU on sequential MNIST, with zero biases, reset-gate scale ar = 0.1 and at most 15 epochs, increasing az improves average training accuracy and reduces epochs to 75% accuracy. Performance is best near ah = 2, and training becomes harder further into the chaotic regime.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization scales controlling GRU gates and recurrent weights affect training speed and accuracy on tasks requiring long temporal dependencies.

fits_no_version.finding: Theoretical analysis and numerical spectra show that GRU update gates and LSTM forget gates create slow dynamical modes; other gates regulate spectral radius. GRU update gates can produce marginal stability in specified parameter regimes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gating controls timescales and local dynamical stability in randomly initialized recurrent networks.

record.peer_reviewed: Mathematical and Scientific Machine Learning, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research vol 107, 2020
record.problems: Training results are described as preliminary and are shown only in Figure 4 without numeric values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The experiment is on sequential MNIST and reports classification accuracy rather than training classification error on CIFAR benchmarks.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were extracted: the only training outcomes relevant to V4 appear only in Figure 4, and the text provides no numeric values; these outcomes also do not measure the initialization behaviors named in V4. The remaining figure panels concern eigenvalue density, outside the claim versions.

untested.parts: Training error in convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and the specified size and training-recipe conditions.
Spurious optimization minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and their dependence on extra student width.
Depth-dependent training degradation in plain convolutional networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts.
Activation-matched initialization and trainable depth in plain networks; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization; very deep plain convolutional networks.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, catapult recovery, and training-loss and curvature dynamics.
Batch-normalization comparisons and normalization-free residual training with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification and V4 tested_not_extracted status should be removed. The training outcomes are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not missing results under the supplied rule. No precise heatmap values can be recovered from the supplied text. The parameters az and ah are initialization scales; their squared values determine weight variances after division by network size.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, optimizer, and the stated effects of early stopping or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious minima frequency, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual networks, depth-dependent training error, and shortcut effects.

The reported figure-only training results concern GRU initialization variance and sequential MNIST accuracy/speed, rather than the version’s feedforward initialization claims about signal propagation, depth, orthogonal weights, or convolutional kernels.
Learning rates above stability thresholds, loss/curvature dynamics, and sharpness.
Batch normalization comparisons, accuracy-speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
